name: AI Worker Workspace
tag: Train a personal AI worker on how you do things, including your wins and mistakes, then hand it real work.

scenarios.title: Teach it how you write proposals
scenarios.ask: Learn from my {samples} past proposals, {=min(wins, samples)} of which won, and draft the next one for a new client.
steps: Read {samples} proposals and noted your structure, pricing style and phrases you use often.
Winning proposals were about {=min(40, 10 + wins * 2)}% shorter and named a start date. Saved that as a rule.
Asked you {=detail * 3} questions about the new client before drafting.
Wrote the proposal in your voice and marked {=4 - detail} spots it wasn't sure about.

result.title: Draft proposal ready
rows: About {=10 + detail * 5} minutes instead of 2 hours

followups: Does it learn from my edits?
Yes. When you change a draft, it asks if the change is a one-off or a new rule, then saves rules to its playbook.
Can I see what it learned?
Everything sits in a plain-English playbook you can read, edit or delete line by line.

scenarios.title: Log a mistake so it never repeats
scenarios.ask: Last month we quoted {jobs} jobs without a travel fee. Teach my worker to catch that.
steps: Recorded the mistake: {jobs} quotes over 20 miles with no travel fee.
Added a rule: any job over 20 miles gets a travel fee line.
Rechecked open quotes and found {=max(1, round(jobs / 2))} with the same gap.
Prepared corrected quotes for your review.
followups: Will it apply this to every quote now?
Yes, every quote it drafts or checks. It will also mention the rule when it adds the fee, so you know why.
What if the rule is wrong sometimes?
Tell it the exception, such as 'not for repeat clients', and it updates the rule.

scenarios.title: Hand it a week of inbox work
scenarios.ask: Take my inbox: about {emails} emails a day. Sort them and draft the replies you're confident about.
steps: Sorted {emails} emails into reply, read later, file and ignore.
Drafted replies for {=round(emails * 0.35)} emails using your past answers.
Held back {=round(emails * 0.08)} it wasn't sure about, with a note on why.
followups: How does it decide what's routine?
Routine means you've answered the same type of email the same way many times. Anything new, emotional or about money stays with you.
Can I take back control quickly?
Yes. One switch drops it back to sort only, and it keeps a log of everything it did.
